City of Abbotsford 2026 PROPERTY TAX NOTICE. total 129,460.47 verified: printed 12x as '2026 TOTAL TAXES & OTHER CHARGES' and 'TOTAL OUTSTANDING TAXES', identical, so nothing is carried forward -- a genuinely large commercial parcel, not a mis-read. payment_due_date from 'DUE DATE: Thursday, July 2, 2026'. || invoice_date is deliberately NOT asserted: this page prints NO issue-date label at all (no Invoice/Billing/Statement/Notice/Issue Date), so build_write_values substitutes date.today() and the run wrote 2026-08-27. `regress.py --add` proposed it as 'stable' only because all three replicates ran on the same day -- a false green that would flip red tomorrow. The defaulting itself is the open A1/A6 defect class, not something this sidecar should lock in. payment_due_date IS asserted because the page prints it explicitly. || account_number ASSERTED AGAIN 2026-09-09, at the user's request. It had been dropped 2026-08-27 because account_number_extract disagreed on FORMATTING only -- '6170066209' vs '61700-6620-9', same digits, a cosmetic normalisation gap (open-defects D2), not a wrong value. That flake is still live: measured 3 of 18 reads across every cached analyzer version. What changed is that the written value no longer comes from that twin. On a property tax notice account_number is taken from folio_number (field_policy.propertytax_account_from_folio), and on all 6 reads of commercial-narrative-v20 the resolution source is 'propertytax_folio' with both folio twins returning '6170066209' -- so the dashed form cannot reach the write while the folio resolves. RESIDUAL RISK, stated once: if the folio resolution ever failed, the substitution would not fire and the dashed account twin could reach the write again. That is not a new exposure, because folio_number is critical on this family, so the same failure would already break the routingDecision assertion above. The folio twins are new in v20, so 6 reads is the whole of the evidence behind them. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free-text summary that rewords every run ('Annual property tax charges for 2026.' vs '2026 property tax notice.'), excluded by the standing rule already recorded on recommend_240124_0001. It was asserted in error when this sidecar was scaffolded from only 3 replicates, all of which happened to agree. || vendor_name IS asserted. The twins return the correct municipality on every read but flip between title case and upper case ('City of Abbotsford' / 'CITY OF ABBOTSFORD'); regress.py compares vendor_name case-insensitively (and suffix-insensitively) for exactly this reason, so the assertion still catches a WRONG vendor while ignoring a difference the pipeline does not promise. The casing itself is open-defects B6a, owned by dataverse-todo DV-4. vendor_name is base-critical and is never dropped from a sidecar. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice. || account_number is written WITHOUT the 'Account No: ' prefix on this family (user requirement, 2026-09-09, propertytax ONLY -- every other municipal bill and every commercial invoice keeps the label).
